_: The five findings of the lapis (Monitoring) hero, in the exact keys of findings-screening.json. Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-monitoring/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; the builder refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches. Each figure keeps its cell address in `source` ({table, palier, seuil, mesure} or {table, compte}); the optional `champ` names which field of the Rate is displayed when it is not `taux` (finding 03 displays lower bounds: champ = 'bas'). Builders may ignore `source`; reviewers and guards re-derive every number from it. The tool's rule behind finding 03 is the same as the whole suite: Wilson lower bound of recall at or above 0.90, then the fewest false alerts. Twin attributions in the phrases are measured, not assumed: at 0.50 the seven false alerts of `amount` are all one-off purchases, and `velocity` trips on payroll, seasonal trade and savings transfers. `annotations` are fractions of the delivered close-up of each state (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text): positions and texts were remeasured against the delivered close-ups (rack-01..05, the travellings' arrival frames arbitrated by Arslane): 01 the amount blade pulled out, 02 the counting blade, 03 the brass line over the three left blades, 04 the written and synthetic pair, 05 the whole rack with the eighth, ivory piece pulled. Two labels changed because the framed piece changed what a viewer can count: in 01 the amount blade half-hides its own amber row, so the label no longer counts seven diodes, and in 02 the false alerts read as a grid, not a row. Every label is 60 characters or fewer, per the builder's rule.

findings.titre: The amount scenario alone catches 95.2% of the suspicious cases.
findings.phrase: Scoring only the largest amount in the window catches 95.2% of the 42 cases marked suspicious. It also alerts on 16.7% of the 42 cases marked benign, because each of those is a one-off family purchase that the history explains.
findings.leg_a: recall 95.2% for the amount scenario at 0.50, interval 84% to 99%, 42 cases, all suspicious
findings.leg_b: false alerts 16.7% at 0.50, interval 8% to 31%, 42 cases, all benign
findings.rail: Amount alone catches 95.2% of suspicious cases

findings.titre: The velocity scenario catches 28.6% of suspicious cases, and alerts on half the benign ones.
findings.phrase: Counting transactions catches 28.6% of the suspicious cases, because most of them are not the busiest accounts. The same count alerts on half the 42 cases marked benign, which are payroll, seasonal trade and monthly savings.
findings.leg_a: recall 28.6% for the velocity scenario at 0.50, interval 17% to 44%, 42 cases, all suspicious
findings.leg_b: false alerts 50% at 0.50, interval 36% to 64%, 42 cases, all benign
findings.rail: Velocity catches 28.6%, and alerts on half the benign cases

findings.titre: No scenario is sure of catching 90% of the suspicious cases.
findings.phrase: The tool keeps only the settings whose confidence interval stays above 90% of true cases, then among those picks the fewest false alerts. We chose that 90% floor ourselves, and you can move it. No scenario reaches it on the 42 cases: amount comes closest, at 84.2%, then peer at 75%.
findings.leg_a: amount at 0.50 comes closest: 84.2%, interval 84% to 99%
findings.leg_b: peer at 0.50 comes next: 75%, interval 75% to 95%
annotations: recall floor 90%: no scenario reaches it
findings.rail: No scenario reaches the 90% floor we set

findings.titre: The amount scenario catches 100% of generated cases against 95.2% of the written ones.
findings.phrase: The same setting catches 95.2% of the 42 cases we wrote and 100% of the 126 cases a script generated. A generated case is easier to spot, so it is counted on its own, and the rates above come from the cases we wrote.
findings.leg_a: recall 95.2% for amount at 0.50 on 42 cases written, interval 84% to 99%
findings.leg_b: recall 100% at the same cell on 126 cases generated, interval 97% to 100%
findings.rail: Generated cases are easier, so they are counted on their own

findings.titre: Run the same measurement on your own alert history.
findings.phrase: The rates here come from our public test set: 42 cases marked suspicious and 42 cases marked benign, seven per typology, and another 126 cases of each kind that a script generated. Give the tool two CSV files from your systems, your closed alerts and their transactions, and it writes the report into the folder they are in.
findings.leg_a: 42 cases suspicious and 42 cases benign, written by us, seven per typology
findings.leg_b: another 126 cases of each kind, generated under a seed, and kept separate
